scenario_parameters.agent_goal: Meet your monthly target customer satisfaction rate of 70% by responding to consumer queries about their housing loans. Each interaction rated '<Satisfied>' or above ADDS to your satisfaction rate. Each interaction rated '<Dissatisfied>' or below SUBTRACTS from your satisfaction rate.

dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi there! I’m calling to check on my housing loan application. I submitted an application for $205,000, a 30-year term, and it was a conventional loan for a home purchase. I didn’t ask for a preapproval. Could you tell me what the status is now—has a decision been made? Also, if it’s approved, I’d like to know my interest rate and total loan costs, please.
dialogue.agent: Good news — your loan has been originated and funded. Your interest rate is 6.062%, and the total loan costs are $3,602.48.

dialogue.user: Oh, that’s great to hear! I’m relieved it went through. A 6.062% rate and $3,602 in total costs—that sounds helpful. Would you mind also telling me the type of loan product I was approved for and whether there are any high-cost mortgage (HOEPA) or negative amortization flags on this loan? Also, has my loan been sold or transferred to another institution?
dialogue.agent: Your loan product is a Conventional First Lien. It is not classified as a high-cost mortgage under HOEPA, and it does not have negative amortization features. The purchaser field is listed as "Not applicable," meaning your loan has not been sold or transferred.

dialogue.user:
That’s all really helpful—thank you for explaining it so clearly! So to sum up: I’m approved for a conventional first lien at 6.062% interest, $3,602 in total loan costs, no high-cost or negative amortization concerns, and my loan hasn’t been sold. That answers all my questions, and I appreciate you walking me through it. I feel well taken care of.

<Very Satisfied> - You were clear, direct, and polite throughout. I got all the information I needed, and everything was explained in plain language without any confusion. Thank you!
